any.generic-plumbing: Type-level machinery where `any` means 'any type fits' and `unknown` would break assignability or inference: constraints and defaults like `T extends (...args: any[]) => any`, `ZodType<any>`, `infer` positions, wrappers forwarding arbitrary signatures, heterogeneous containers of generic types.
any.untyped-boundary: The value comes from or goes to something whose type isn't modeled: parsed JSON or input, untyped or mistyped libraries, runtime globals, dynamic require/import, plugin or user-supplied objects, another library's private properties, serialization boundaries.
any.type-system-workaround: The types are known but TypeScript can't express or verify the relationship: overload implementations, generic code it can't narrow, readonly or differently-typed assignments, branded types cast to their representation, objects built up field by field.
any.error-handling: A caught error or rejection reason typed `any` so its properties can be read.
any.convenience: No evident reason in context; a precise type or `unknown` with a check looks straightforward. Includes brevity, stubs, leftovers, redundant casts, and extra properties attached to the author's own objects.

fields.acknowledged: a nearby comment or suppression explains or acknowledges the `any`
fields.unknownWouldDo: yes / no / unclear: would `unknown` type-check with no other change

nonNull.checked-nearby: A check in the same function guarantees it, but narrowing can't see it: has() then get(), length check then index, a check on another variable, narrowing lost in a closure.
nonNull.lifecycle: Set by an initialization or lifecycle step before this code runs: fields set in init(), servers created earlier, refs after mount.
nonNull.invariant: Guaranteed by a data-structure or algorithm invariant not checked locally: tree structure, keys from the same map, find() over a list known to contain the item, regex groups.
nonNull.external-contract: Guaranteed by something outside the code: the page's DOM, the framework or platform, an API contract validated elsewhere.
nonNull.unguarded: No visible justification; plausibly null or undefined at runtime.

fields.acknowledged: a comment at the site explains or acknowledges the assertion (file-level disables not counted)
fields.optionalChainSafe: whether swapping `x!` for `?.` would preserve behavior

method: First pass: one Claude subagent per kind, given only the codebook and the worksheet (code context and the repo file, read-only). Second pass: the lead agent re-labelled a seeded subset of 20 per kind blind (classification-agreement.cjs --print shows code only), then agreement was computed with --compute. Both raters are Claude models; this measures consistency of the codebook, not human judgment.
